caveats: **DISM is process-global and single-session.** The Windows DISM API does not support concurrent sessions safely from the same process; every `list`/`info` call is serialised through agent-core's process-global `DismSlot` (at most one DISM call in flight), reporting `windows:dism:busy` to a second caller rather than risking undefined concurrent-session behaviour.

**A timed-out call is `abandoned`, not cleared, until the worker returns.** If `DismGetFeatures`/`DismGetFeatureInfo` exceeds the 17s bounded timeout, the dispatching thread reports `windows:dism:timeout` and marks the slot abandoned; every subsequent call reports `windows:dism:abandoned` until the original worker thread actually finishes and releases the slot — permanently, if DISM itself never returns, cleared only by a service restart.

**Pending states come from the feature enum, not a reboot-pending registry key.** `pending_enable`/`pending_disable` reflect `DismPackageFeatureState`'s `InstallPending`/`UninstallPending` values as reported by DISM itself, not an independent reboot-pending check.

**Feature names are DISM's internal names, not Control Panel labels.** `NetFx3`, `SMB1Protocol`, `TelnetClient` etc. are the `FeatureName` DISM uses internally; the `info` action's `display_name` field carries the operator-visible label.

**The macOS/Linux rows are placeholders by design.** DISM has no equivalent on either platform — both legs return the honest `unsupported` row unconditionally, never an empty read or a fabricated value.

definitions.description: Detail for one Windows optional OS feature (DismGetFeatureInfo): its display name, description, state, and restart requirement. `feature` is bounded and character-restricted (`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,256}$`) before it ever reaches DISM — an invalid value is refused with no DISM call. Windows-only: DISM has no Linux/macOS equivalent.

Enumerates Windows optional OS features (DismGetFeatures) and reports each one's state — enabled, disabled, pending_enable, pending_disable, superseded, partially_installed, or unknown — plus whether a restart is required to complete a pending change. An optional `state` filter narrows to one bucket (enabled = installed only; disabled = not present/removed/staged; pending = install/uninstall pending). Windows-only: DISM has no Linux/macOS equivalent.

description: Windows optional OS feature state (enabled/disabled/pending) via the DISM API
how_it_works:
Both actions run the same DISM session lifecycle, in order, entirely inside one bounded call on a worker thread: acquire agent-core's process-global slot (`DismSlot`, at most one DISM call in flight at a time) → `DismInitialize` → `DismOpenSession(DISM_ONLINE_IMAGE)` → `DismGetFeatures` (`list`) or `DismGetFeatureInfo` (`info`) → map each `DismPackageFeatureState`/`DismRestartType` int to a named state → `DismCloseSession` → `DismShutdown` → release the slot. `DismApi.dll` is never linked; its eight exports are resolved once at runtime from `System32` (see the source header comment for why). The dispatching thread only ever tries to acquire the slot and waits on the bounded call — the DISM session lifecycle, the slot, and the bounded-call wrapping itself all live in agent-core (never unloaded), not this plugin, so a worker that outlives this plugin's own shutdown quiesce never executes plugin-resident code.

**What it is NOT.** No enable, disable, add, remove or commit — the eight resolved exports are the plugin's whole DISM surface, and none of them mutates. No `dism.exe` subprocess: everything is an in-process API call. No WMI: `Win32_OptionalFeature` is not used.

outputs_note: Pipe-delimited rows via `write_output()`. `list` writes one `feature|` row per feature (or per matching feature when `state` filters); `info` writes exactly one `feature_info|` row. On an unsupported or unavailable leg, both actions instead write a single sentinel row: `feature|unsupported|<os>:dism:unsupported` / `feature|unavailable|windows:dism:<token>` (or the `feature_info` equivalent for `info`) — never a blank or omitted row.

result_status.when: a clean `list`/`info` read — the DISM call succeeded and the feature row(s) were written
`DismApi.dll` or one of its eight required exports could not be resolved from `System32`
Linux/macOS: DISM has no equivalent on this platform
`info`: the named feature does not exist (`DismGetFeatureInfo` returns `DISMAPI_E_UNKNOWN_FEATURE`)
another DISM call already holds the plugin's in-process slot, or the bounded-call outstanding-call ceiling rejected this call before it started
a previous call timed out and its worker has not returned; the DISM API is still held by that worker until it does
`DismGetFeatures`/`DismGetFeatureInfo` did not return within the 17s bounded timeout
a DISM session-lifecycle call failed with a non-access-denied HRESULT
an unhandled exception was caught inside the bounded DISM call
a DISM call in the session returned `E_ACCESSDENIED` — the caller's token lacks the elevated privilege the DISM API requires

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result only.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore (`response_retention_days`, default 90 days), queryable at `/api/responses/{id}` and aggregatable (`list` groups by `state`, counted).
**Not consumed by** daily-sync inventory, the TAR warehouse, DEX, or metrics. `gather.ttlSeconds: 300` only caps how often a repeat dispatch is served from cache; nothing runs on a schedule.

**Sensitivity.** Rows name which built-in Windows OS features are enabled on the device (e.g. `SMB1Protocol`, `TelnetClient`) — a security-relevant configuration signal, but no username, hostname, serial number or file path appears in any field.

**Siblings:** `msi_packages` (installed third-party/MSI software, not OS features), `windows_updates` (patch history, not feature toggles), `registry`/`wmi` (general-purpose Windows reads this plugin's narrow DISM surface deliberately does not replace) — none join with this plugin's output.

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) → `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) → `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("windows.features.list")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/responses/{id}`.
